title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript note from the divided-power de Rham material on the neighbouring pages. It is page 59 of the typescript of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie', Grothendieck), filed in cote 136. The archive stamp reads 377 and the header reads IX.

Setting: S is a trait (spectrum of a discrete valuation ring) with fraction field K and residue field k of characteristic p. A_K is an abelian variety over K with semi-stable reduction, and A'_K is its dual. Let A_o^o and A'^o_o be the identity components of the special fibres of the Néron models. By semi-stability each is an extension of an abelian variety (B_o, resp. B'_o) by a torus.

The Néron-model biextension W of (A^o, A'^o) by G_m (from IX 1.4) restricts on the special fibre to a biextension W_o of (A_o^o, A'^o_o) by G_m. By VIII 4.8, W_o descends, uniquely up to unique isomorphism, to a biextension W_o^ab of the abelian parts (B_o, B'_o). A biextension of two abelian varieties by G_m is the same as a divisorial correspondence, so it defines a homomorphism B_o → D(B'_o) (5.3.7). By IX 1.5 this map has finite kernel and is an isogeny.

The ℓ-adic pairing (5.3.5) on Tate modules is induced by W_o^ab. The associated map T_ℓ(B_o) → T_ℓ(D(B'_o)) (5.3.6) is T_ℓ applied to (5.3.7). Hence perfectness of the pairing for ℓ ≠ p is equivalent to the kernel of the isogeny having trivial ℓ-primary part; this is the standard dictionary of Mumford's Abelian Varieties, reference [5].

The preceding arguments therefore show only that the kernel is a p-group. Theorem 5.4 then states the full result: W_o^ab is a perfect duality between B_o and B'_o, i.e. the abelian part of the dual is the dual of the abelian part, including at p. The proof, which handles p, comes on later pages.

The purpose is the study of the monodromy pairing and orthogonality theorems for semistable abelian varieties in SGA 7 IX.
errors: The statement says 'A_K un schéma abélien sur S'; it should read 'sur K' (an abelian variety over the generic point). This is a typo or slip in the typescript.

There is no mathematical error. The argument on this page establishes only the prime-to-p part of the duality; the p-part requires the further argument promised in the theorem's proof, and the text says so explicitly.

ideas.what: A biextension of extensions of abelian varieties by tori, with values in G_m, descends uniquely to a biextension of the abelian parts.
ideas.modern_name: Descent of biextensions to abelian parts (SGA 7 VIII 4.8)

ideas.what: Perfectness of the ℓ-adic pairing is equivalent to the vanishing of the ℓ-part of the kernel of the isogeny B_o → D(B'_o).
ideas.modern_name: Weil pairing / Tate module dictionary for isogenies

ideas.what: Theorem 5.4: the abelian parts of the Néron models of A_K and of its dual are dual abelian varieties via the canonical biextension (semi-stable case), including at p.
ideas.modern_name: Duality of abelian parts of Néron models (Grothendieck)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 IX, containing the statement of Theorem 5.4, which is well known and credited to Grothendieck. Nothing on it is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: This page belongs to the SGA 7 IX typescript, not to the divided-power de Rham notes on the neighbouring pages; it appears to be misfiled or reused paper within cote 136.
In (5.3.7) the target is D(B'_o); the prime is a blue-ink manual correction on the typescript.
'un schéma abélien sur S' is as typed, but the sense requires 'sur K'.
The handwritten '377' at the bottom is the archive pagination, and '196' in the margin is the scan's page index.
